title: Cyrus and the Hollow Revisited
premise: Jonah Dravenmoor, the last swordspeaker, has hidden his magic for five years in the anti-magical city of Vell, finding fragile happiness with a cartographer named Wren. When Wren's face appears in a century-old prophecy book, Jonah learns the court beneath the mountain has purchased Wren's soul as payment for a debt incurred by Jonah's own dead order. To reclaim it, Jonah must break his final oath, descend into the Hollow, and confront the sovereign who holds every oath he ever swore. In the end, Jonah shatters the covenant that binds all swordspeakers—losing his magic but winning Wren's soul back, and choosing an ordinary life over power.
about_author: Sebastian Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about quiet people forced into loud destinies, and live somewhere rainy with too many annotated maps.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Tuesday
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A quiet evening selling minor charms in Vell's night market, establishing his careful invisibility and his tender, cautious romance with Wren, a mapmaker who suspects more than she says. The emotional beat is contentment shadowed by guilt—the sense that happiness this good must be borrowed.

chapters.title: A Face in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A dying collector trades Jonah a prophecy book for one last charm; inside, a woodcut dated 112 years ago shows Wren standing before the mountain gate. Jonah's denial curdles into dread as he realizes the prophecy names her soul as 'the court's due.' Beat: vertigo—the past has been waiting for them.

chapters.title: What Wren Already Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Confronted, Wren reveals she has dreamed of the mountain since childhood and once signed something she cannot remember signing. Her fear is not of fate but of losing herself. The beat is intimacy deepening through shared terror—they choose each other knowingly, which raises the stakes.

chapters.title: The Debt of the Ninth Order
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah seeks out Maren, his former mentor turned drunk, and learns the truth: his oath-bound order sold a hundred souls to the Hollow to end a war, and Wren's is the final installment coming due. Beat: shame—his order's sin, his inheritance.

chapters.title: Breaking the First Seal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. City wardens raid the market hunting unlicensed magic after someone informs on Jonah. Wren burns her own beloved maps to destroy evidence, sacrificing her art to protect him. Beat: love against duty made literal—she chooses him over everything she built.

chapters.title: The Road Under the World
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Fleeing Vell, the pair follow Maren's directions into the underways, where Jonah's suppressed swordspeech begins waking painfully, each word costing blood. They are hunted by a Hollow herald wearing the face of Jonah's dead brother. Beat: the past weaponized against him.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the Hollow's glittering court, where souls hang like lanterns and the Sovereign offers Jonah a bargain: his own soul and restored power in exchange for Wren's. Jonah nearly accepts. Beat: temptation—power offered at exactly the price of love.

chapters.title: Oathbreaker
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Imprisoned, Jonah speaks the forbidden Unbinding—a swordspeech that dissolves oaths rather than enforcing them—shattering the ancient covenant and freeing every hung soul, including his brother's shade, who forgives him. Beat: climax; corruption refused, identity reclaimed through destruction of the old self.

chapters.title: The Long Way Up
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. As the Hollow collapses, Wren guides the freed, half-remembering souls toward daylight, carrying an exhausted, now-magicless Jonah. She realizes she loves him most without the sword in his voice. Beat: tenderness after ruin; duty fulfilled not by power but by care.

chapters.title: Maps Without Magic
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Months later, Jonah sells honest trinkets while Wren draws new maps of the reopened underways; the prophecy book's final page now shows only two blank figures walking. Quiet, earned peace—the story ends where it began, but chosen rather than hidden. Beat: resolution and hope.
